beliefs.practice: Read the MongoDB connection string from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) and configure Mongoose to use the unified topology, a bounded connection pool (e.g. maxPoolSize: 50), and a serverSelectionTimeoutMS to fail fast; never embed credentials in code or config files.

Require TLS/SSL for all connections (use tls=true / ssl=true in the connection string or Mongoose tls options) and validate the server certificate (set rejectUnauthorized: true or provide CA file) so credentials and vectors are sent encrypted.

Never log or store the cluster connection string, LLM API keys, or other secrets; keep a .env.example with placeholders and use a secrets manager (Azure Key Vault or environment variables) for runtime secrets.

Use a least-privilege database account for the app (create a Mongo user with only the required roles/privileges for the sample database) and rotate credentials regularly rather than using a master key.
Partition documents so that all versions of an asset share the same partition key (use assetId as partition key) to keep versioned documents colocated and avoid cross-partition aggregation costs.
Create a compound index on { assetId: 1, version: -1, createdAt: -1 } to efficiently query the latest version(s) per asset and support range queries over versions by createdAt.
Index fields used for LLM-derived classification and aggregation (e.g., type, eligibilityTier) with single-field or compound indexes to speed the coverage-ratio aggregation pipeline.

If using vectors, avoid indexing the raw high-dimensional vector field with standard B-tree indexes; instead rely on the platform's vector-index feature (DiskANN/HNSW/IVF) and keep vector dimension and dtype consistent across documents.

Do vector indexing configuration out-of-band (via the cluster/index tools) specifying algorithm (HNSW/IVF), M or efConstruction for HNSW, and ensure the index's dimension matches stored vectors; do not attempt to create such indexes via naive schema mappings.

Implement optimistic concurrency for versioned documents (use a version field or Mongoose versionKey and include it in update predicates or use findOneAndUpdate with a condition on version) rather than relying on multi-document transactions.

Store each collateral asset version as an append-only document (version and createdAt fields) and consider maintaining a lightweight 'current' document (either in the same collection with a flag or in a separate collection) to speed reads for current state.

Use server-side aggregation pipelines (db.collection.aggregate) for computing totals and coverage ratios instead of loading all documents into the application; craft the pipeline to filter by partition key to avoid cross-partition scans.
Handle 429/RequestRateTooLarge by implementing retries with exponential backoff and honoring any Retry-After or x-ms-retry-after-ms response header values returned by the service.

Monitor and plan RU/s consumption for the aggregation and vector search operations; use explain() on heavy aggregation pipelines to estimate RU cost and add appropriate indexes or filters to reduce RU usage.
Make seed scripts idempotent by using upsert operations keyed by a natural unique key (assetId + version) or by checking for existence before insert so repeated runs do not duplicate versions.

Protect LLM classification step and its API key: call the LLM from a backend service (not client-side), cache classification results on the document, and never persist raw LLM prompts or API keys in the database.

Create TTL indexes if you need to automatically expire old history documents (e.g., ttlSeconds on createdAt) but only after verifying RU impact and retention policies; do not rely on TTL for critical audit history unless policy allows.

Limit indexed fields and use sparse/partial indexes for optional LLM-derived fields (e.g., eligibilityTier) to reduce index size and RU costs; avoid indexing large text or vector fields with general-purpose indexes.

Use readPreference=primary for read-after-write consistency when immediately reading a just-written version; otherwise use appropriate read preferences but be aware of eventual consistency semantics and their effect on coverage calculations.

Keep connection pool sizes and concurrent query counts tuned to the RU budget and the cluster's connection limits; close the Mongoose connection gracefully on process exit to avoid leaking connections.

When aggregating coverage ratio, design the pipeline to push filters and projections early (use $match on partition key/asset type, then $group) so the work is reduced and indexes can be used; use $project to include only numeric fields used in sums.
Use testing practices that mock the DB and LLM for unit tests (so tests run offline) and include a small integration/seeding step keyed behind an environment flag for live-cluster verification only.
